regions.title: Commitments & governing law
regions.description: Identify the undertaking and the body of law that applies.
regions.routeQuestion: What was promised, and which law applies?

districts.title: What is the commitment?
districts.question: Read the assurance in its factual setting.

districts.title: When does Article 2 apply?
districts.question: Locate the goods, services, and relevant merchant status.

districts.title: Consequences of formation
districts.question: Track the particular right that depends on a contract.

regions.title: Consideration
regions.description: Move from the requested exchange to its sufficiency and limits.

districts.title: Bargained-for exchange
districts.question: What was sought and given in return?

districts.title: Sufficiency of the exchange
districts.question: Separate value, genuine exchange, and past action.

districts.title: Forbearance & settlement
districts.question: What claim or freedom did the promisee surrender?

districts.title: Discretion & implied obligations
districts.question: Identify the constraint on satisfaction, quantity, or effort.
principalCases: Structural Polymer Group, Ltd. v. Zoltek Corp.

regions.title: Reliance & restitution
regions.description: Distinguish induced changes of position from benefits received.
regions.routeQuestion: If not, did someone rely on it, or get enriched?

districts.title: Promissory estoppel
districts.question: Which promise induced which change of position?

districts.title: Reliance in particular settings
districts.question: Keep the promise, the injury, and the available relief distinct.
principalCases: D & G Stout, Inc. v. Bacardi Imports, Inc.

districts.title: Unjust enrichment
districts.question: Identify the benefit and why its retention is in question.

regions.title: Assent & intent
regions.description: Examine the communicated agreement, context, and notice.

districts.title: Objective assent
districts.question: What did the words and conduct reasonably communicate?

districts.title: Intent to be legally bound
districts.question: Locate the role of social context or a reserved writing.

districts.title: Notice & consumer terms
districts.question: When and how were the terms presented?

regions.title: Offer
regions.description: Find the offer, then determine how long it can be accepted.
regions.routeQuestion: Was there an offer, and is it still open?

districts.title: Was there an offer?
districts.question: Identify a commitment that the recipient can accept.

districts.title: Advertisements & rewards
districts.question: Read quantity, audience, and the invited response.
principalCases: Lefkowitz v. Great Minneapolis Surplus Store

districts.title: Lapse, revocation & other endings
districts.question: Distinguish expiry, withdrawal, and the terminating event.

districts.title: Options & protected offers
districts.question: Separate the protection against revocation from acceptance itself.

regions.title: Acceptance
regions.description: Identify the responsive act, the invited method, and its timing.
regions.routeQuestion: Was it accepted, how, and when?

districts.title: Promise, conduct & performance
districts.question: Does the response commit to the offer?

districts.title: Performance or preparation?
districts.question: Ask what role the act plays in this particular offer.

districts.title: Notification of acceptance
districts.question: Distinguish acceptance from communication of that acceptance.
principalCases: International Filter Co. v. Conroe Gin, Ice & Light Co.

districts.title: Silence & established dealings
districts.question: Identify the conduct or prior practice beyond silence.

districts.title: The mailbox rule
districts.question: Place dispatch, receipt, and competing communications in order.

regions.title: Formalities
regions.description: Separate substitutes for consideration from writing requirements.
regions.routeQuestion: Does a writing or a seal matter?

districts.title: Form & consideration
districts.question: Identify what work a seal, writing, or recital is doing.

districts.title: Statute of Frauds
districts.question: Locate coverage, the required writing, and the stated exceptions.
principalCases: Tolosa v. HSBC Bank USA, N.A.

regions.title: Terms & battle of forms
regions.description: Separate whether a contract formed from which terms belong to it.
regions.routeQuestion: Which terms made it in when forms clash?

districts.title: Common-law responses
districts.question: Distinguish counteroffer, inquiry, and the effect of performance.

districts.title: The § 2-207 sequence
districts.question: Start with formation before selecting the terms.

districts.title: Formation by writings · § 2-207(1)
districts.question: Identify the consequence of an expressly conditional response.

districts.title: Formation by conduct · § 2-207(3)
districts.question: Do both parties recognize a contract despite the failure of their writings?
principalCases: C. Itoh & Co. (America) Inc. v. Jordan International Co.

districts.title: Additional terms
districts.question: Apply the merchant and material-alteration questions.
principalCases: Bayway Refining Co. v. Oxygenated Marketing & Trading A.G.

districts.title: Different terms
districts.question: Keep the competing approaches and jurisdictional prediction distinct.

regions.title: Remedies
regions.description: Choose the protected interest, then examine the form of relief.
regions.routeQuestion: What can the injured party get?

districts.title: Protected interests
districts.question: Distinguish expectation, reliance, restitution, and gains.
principalCases: United States Naval Institute v. Charter Communications, Inc.

districts.title: Specific relief
districts.question: Examine adequacy of money and the proposed order.

districts.title: Nominal, actual & punitive relief
districts.question: Identify what an award compensates or recognizes.

districts.title: Economics & enforcement in practice
districts.question: Read the model and the institutional assumptions separately.

regions.title: Negotiations & incomplete agreements
regions.description: Explore the questions, then read the cases and their course-wide connections.
regions.routeQuestion: Is an unfinished deal a deal?

districts.title: Commitments during negotiation
districts.question: Negotiations can create limited legal obligations before the parties form the final contract they are discussing. The obligation may arise from a specific assurance or an agreement about how to negotiate.
principalCases: Channel Home Centers, Division of Grace Retail Corp. v. Grossman
Cyberchron Corp. v. Calldata Systems Development, Inc.

districts.title: Sufficiently definite obligations
districts.question: Definiteness concerns whether the parties’ commitment is clear enough for a court to identify the obligation, determine breach, and provide a remedy. An open term can sometimes be supplied without defeating the agreement.
principalCases: Oglebay Norton Co. v. Armco, Inc.
Sun Printing & Publishing Ass’n v. Remington Paper & Power Co.

districts.title: International sales and the CISG
districts.question: The CISG is the United Nations treaty on contracts for qualifying international sales of goods. Its own provisions can govern a sale instead of the domestic sales rules a reader might otherwise assume apply.
principalCases: TeeVee Toons, Inc. v. Gerhard Schubert GmbH

regions.title: Modifying & policing agreement
regions.description: Explore the questions, then read the cases and their course-wide connections.
regions.routeQuestion: Can the deal be changed, and was it fairly made?

districts.title: Changing an existing agreement
districts.question: A modification changes duties under an existing contract. Identify the proposed change and the governing law before deciding whether new consideration, good faith, a writing, or assent is required.

districts.title: Threats and practical alternatives
districts.question: Duress asks whether an improper threat induced agreement when the affected party lacked a reasonable alternative. Severe commercial pressure requires examination of its source, timing, and available responses.
principalCases: Austin Instrument, Inc. v. Loral Corporation

districts.title: False statements and misleading conduct
districts.question: Misrepresentation concerns a false or misleading representation that affects a party’s decision to agree. Analyze what was represented, why it was misleading, how it induced assent, and whether reliance was justified under the applicable rule.
principalCases: Psenicska v. Twentieth Century Fox Film Corp.

districts.title: When information must be disclosed
districts.question: Disclosure rules determine when a party must reveal information rather than remain silent. A party that chooses to speak may need to supply enough information to keep its statements from becoming misleading.

regions.title: Interpreting the agreement
regions.description: Explore the questions, then read the cases and their course-wide connections.
regions.routeQuestion: What do the words mean, and what evidence counts?

districts.title: Writing and prior agreements
districts.question: The parol evidence rule determines how a final written agreement affects alleged earlier or contemporaneous agreements. It addresses the legal effect of a writing, not simply whether a witness may speak about it.
principalCases: Bollinger v. Central Pennsylvania Quarry Stripping and Construction Co.
Gianni v. R. Russel & Co., Inc.

districts.title: Meaning in context
districts.question: Interpretation determines the meaning and scope of the parties’ agreement. It asks what their words and conduct mean in the relevant setting, including the evidence the governing law permits the court to consider.
principalCases: Pacific Gas & Electric Co. v. G.W. Thomas Drayage & Rigging Co.
Trident Center v. Connecticut General Life Insurance Co.

districts.title: Trade and the parties’ dealings
districts.question: A trade usage is a sufficiently established practice in a business that helps determine what parties in that setting reasonably understand their agreement to mean or require.
principalCases: Columbia Nitrogen Corp. v. Royster Co.
Figgie International, Inc. v. Destileria Serralles, Inc.
Frigaliment Importing Co. v. B.N.S. International Sales Corp.
Nanakuli Paving & Rock Co. v. Shell Oil Co.

districts.title: Discretion, efforts, and good faith
districts.question: Contractual discretion is a party’s power to make a choice affecting performance, such as whether a result is satisfactory, how much to order, or how strongly to promote a product. The question is what limits govern that choice.
principalCases: Ng Giap Hon v. Westcomb Securities Pte Ltd and Others

regions.title: Limits on contractual terms
regions.description: Explore the questions, then read the cases and their course-wide connections.
regions.routeQuestion: Which terms will the law refuse to enforce?

districts.title: Standard forms and expected terms
districts.question: An adhesion contract is a standardized agreement presented by a party with superior bargaining power on terms the other party can generally accept or reject rather than negotiate.
principalCases: Klar v. H. & M. Parcel Room, Inc.

districts.title: Consumer protection
districts.question: Consumer-protection statutes can impose requirements and remedies even when ordinary rules of assent and consideration would recognize a contract.

districts.title: Unconscionable bargains
districts.question: Unconscionability examines whether the circumstances of agreement and the substance of its terms make enforcement impermissibly unfair under the governing rule.

districts.title: Enforcement and public policy
districts.question: Public-policy rules can limit enforcement of an agreement because of interests the law protects beyond the parties’ private exchange.
principalCases: Blossom Farm Products Co. v. Kasson Cheese Co., Inc.
X.L.O. Concrete Corp. v. Rivergate Corp.

districts.title: Restrictions on competition
districts.question: A noncompetition covenant limits a worker’s or business seller’s ability to compete after a relationship ends. Its enforceability requires the particular governing restrictions and the scope of the restraint to be examined.

regions.title: Performance & conditions
regions.description: Explore the questions, then read the cases and their course-wide connections.
regions.routeQuestion: Who had to perform first, and did they?

districts.title: Express conditions and satisfaction
districts.question: An express condition is an event the parties specify must occur before a duty becomes due, or whose occurrence affects that duty as the agreement provides.
principalCases: Peacock Construction Co. v. Modern Air Conditioning, Inc.

districts.title: The order of performance
districts.question: A constructive condition is a dependency the law recognizes between the parties’ performances even when the agreement does not expressly use conditional language.

districts.title: Substantial performance and defects
districts.question: Substantial performance can permit recovery of the contract price, with an adjustment for defects, where the party has performed the essential undertaking and the remaining departure does not justify treating the exchange as failed.

districts.title: Dividing the exchange
districts.question: A divisible contract separates agreed performances into corresponding parts, so a party’s right to payment for one completed part may be assessed independently of unperformed parts.

districts.title: Waiver, prevention, and forfeiture
districts.question: Waiver concerns a party’s decision or conduct giving up the right to insist on a contractual requirement, including a condition placed for that party’s protection.

regions.title: Measuring and limiting relief
regions.description: Explore the questions, then read the cases and their course-wide connections.
regions.routeQuestion: How is that measured, and where does it stop?

districts.title: Completion cost and performance value
districts.question: These measures compare the cost of obtaining the promised performance with the reduction in the property’s value caused by the defect. The governing rule decides which better protects the contractual entitlement in the circumstances.
principalCases: Peevyhouse v. Garland Coal & Mining Co.

districts.title: Avoidable loss
districts.question: Mitigation limits recovery for loss the injured party could reasonably have avoided after breach. It ordinarily concerns the recoverable amount rather than imposing a separate duty to perform for the breacher’s benefit.
principalCases: Parker v. Twentieth Century-Fox Film Corp.
Rockingham County v. Luten Bridge Co.

districts.title: Foreseeable consequences
districts.question: Foreseeability limits which consequences of breach can be charged to the breaching party by reference to the circumstances and information at the time of contracting.
principalCases: Kenford Co. v. County of Erie

districts.title: Proving the amount of loss
districts.question: The certainty requirement asks whether evidence supports the existence and amount of the claimed loss sufficiently for an award. It does not always require exact arithmetic or an established business history.

districts.title: Agreed damages and penalties
districts.question: A stipulated remedy specifies consequences of breach in advance. Courts distinguish enforceable compensation arrangements from penalties under the governing law, and the parties’ label is not conclusive.
principalCases: Lake River Corp. v. Carborundum Co.
Swiss Federal Supreme Court: contractual penalty decision of September 24, 2024
Wasserman’s Inc. v. Township of Middletown

districts.title: Restitution after breach
districts.question: The restitution interest concerns restoration of benefits conferred on another party, rather than the full value of expected performance or every loss incurred in reliance.
principalCases: United States v. Algernon Blair, Inc.
Walgreen Co. v. Sara Creek Property Co.

regions.title: Mistaken assumptions & changed events
regions.description: Explore the questions, then read the cases and their course-wide connections.
regions.routeQuestion: Does mistake or a changed world excuse performance?

districts.title: Mistake and allocated risks
districts.question: Mistake concerns an erroneous belief about facts existing when the agreement is made. Relief depends on the significance of that assumption and who bears the risk that it is wrong.

districts.title: Impracticability and force majeure
districts.question: Impossibility and impracticability doctrines address circumstances in which an event prevents or severely disrupts the promised performance and the governing law may excuse it.
principalCases: Transatlantic Financing Corp. v. United States

districts.title: Frustration of the agreed purpose
districts.question: Frustration concerns an event that destroys the principal purpose of the exchange for a party even though the promised performance may remain physically possible.

regions.title: Third-party rights & transfers
regions.description: Explore the questions, then read the cases and their course-wide connections.
regions.routeQuestion: Who else can enforce or take over the deal?

districts.title: Intended beneficiaries and their rights
districts.question: A third-party beneficiary is someone who may claim a benefit under a contract made by other people. The key question is whether the agreement and governing law give that person an enforceable right rather than merely an incidental advantage.

districts.title: Beneficiaries of public contracts
districts.question: A person who benefits from a government contract does not necessarily acquire a private contractual right to enforce it.

districts.title: Assignment and delegation
districts.question: Assignment transfers a contractual right from its holder to another person. The assignee seeks the transferred benefit, while the underlying agreement determines what the obligor must provide.

regions.description: Explore the questions, then read the cases and their course-wide connections.
